characterList.description: Bald man with glasses, wearing a black velvet jacket and a black and white patterned shirt. He holds a tablet.
characterList.name: Presenter

characterList.description: Asian man with short black hair, wearing a red polo shirt. Holds a piece of paper with a colored spectrum.
characterList.name: Dong-Seon Chang

content_metadata.description: A video presentation by Dong-Seon Chang discussing the impact of social interaction on human perception and happiness, supported by scientific evidence and interactive discussions.

qAndA.answer: He asks them to identify a color on a spectrum between green and blue, specifically a shade that most people would perceive as blue.
qAndA.question: What color does Dong-Seon Chang ask the participants in the experiment to identify?

qAndA.answer: He utilizes the concept of 'adaptation,' where prolonged exposure to a color affects subsequent color perception.
qAndA.question: What method does Dong-Seon Chang use to determine if the participants are genuinely perceiving the color they claim to see?
What is the name of the simple game referenced by Dong-Seon Chang that highlights the power of social feedback?

qAndA.answer: Humans have the largest neocortex, allowing for complex thought and social interaction.
qAndA.question: According to the research Dong-Seon Chang presents, what makes humans special compared to other living beings?

qAndA.answer: The Dunbar number suggests humans can maintain around 150 meaningful relationships.
qAndA.question: What is the approximate number of meaningful relationships that humans can maintain, according to the Dunbar number?
